knowledge_point.title: Projecting a Vector Onto a Perpendicular Vector

question.:question/problem:
Given that the angle between the nonzero vectors $a$ and $b$ is $90^\circ$, find the scalar projection of $a$ onto $b.$

{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{comp}_{b}\,a & =|a|\cos\theta \\ & =|a|\cos(90^\circ) \\ & =|a|\cdot 0 \\ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $p$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $q$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
p⊥q\,⟹\,p\cdot q=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & ={p}_{x}\cdot {q}_{x}+{p}_{y}\cdot {q}_{y}+{p}_{z}\cdot {q}_{z} \\  & =3\cdot x+(-6)\cdot 3+(-2)\cdot 2 \\  & =3x-22.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & =0 \\ 3x-22 & =0 \\ 3x & =22 \\ x & =\frac{22}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
